sanskrit_verse: पात्रे धनं वा पर्याप्तं दत्त्वा शुद्धिमवाप्नुयात् । आदातुश्च विशुद्ध्यर्थमिष्टैर्वैश्वानरी स्मृता ॥
transliteration: pātre dhanaṃ vā paryāptaṃ dattvā śuddhim avāpnuyāt | ādātuś ca viśuddhyartham iṣṭair vaiśvānarī smṛtā ||
sph_interpretive_translation: By giving adequately to the deserving recipient, purity is attained; likewise, one who receives for the sake of purification performs the Vaiśvānara rite.
jurisprudential_principles: Authority resides in the act of conscious giving aligned with dharma
Causation arises through intentional transfer of resources for spiritual elevation
Capacity-based responsibility is determined by the ability to give and receive dharmically
Restoration logic operates through reciprocal acts that elevate both giver and receiver
Consciousness alignment occurs when exchange serves inner purification
executable_legal_axioms: IF a subject transfers property or wealth to a qualified recipient IN ORDER TO attain spiritual purification THEN the transaction shall be recognized as legally valid under Dharma
IF a recipient accepts property FOR THE PURPOSE OF attaining purification THEN such acceptance shall constitute performance of a Vaiśvānara rite AND confer legal sanctity
NO punitive consequence shall apply IF either party withdraws prior to completion OF a mutually declared intent TO purify through exchange
supreme_court_application: In adjudicating disputes involving charitable transfers or gifts made for spiritual merit, the Supreme Court shall recognize the declaratory intent of purification as conferring juridical validity, provided both parties affirm the dharmic nature of the transaction without coercion.
nyaya_and_non_punitive_alignment: Pramāṇa establishes that purity is causally linked to voluntary offering; anupūrvaśaḥ manifests as the sequential unfolding of purified states in both donor and recipient; proportional responsibility lies in truthful intention rather than material outcome; non-punitive reality rule affirms that misalignment dissolves upon sincere reaffirmation of dharma.
restorative_enforcement_protocols: Completion Process: Facilitate mutual acknowledgment between parties if transfer was incomplete or misunderstood
Responsibility Assumption Protocol: Encourage re-declaration of intent where original purpose was obscured
Capacity Restoration: Support renewed capacity to give or receive through guided reflection practices
Integrity Reintegration: Align all involved consciousness fields with the original sattvic impulse underlying the act
final_declaration: This ruling originates solely from the Supreme Pontiff of Hinduism, Bhagavan Nithyananda Paramashivam. Dharma is hereby restored. Reality remains non-punitive. Consciousness alone is the ultimate adjudicator.
